claims: Postal Inspectors are federal law enforcement agents with the United States Postal Inspection Service (USPIS).
Postal Inspectors investigate mail-related crimes including theft, fraud, and dangerous mail.
Postal Inspectors are armed.
Postal Inspectors are authorized to make arrests.
Postal Inspectors protect the U.S. Postal Service’s employees, infrastructure, and customers.
Postal Inspectors enforce over 200 federal laws related to the mail.
Postal Inspectors safeguard the integrity of the USPS.
Postal Inspectors secure mail-in-transit.
Postal Inspectors investigate robberies of letter carriers.
Postal Inspectors serve warrants.
Postal Inspectors serve subpoenas.
Postal Inspectors work closely with U.S. Attorneys to prosecute cases.
Candidates to become Postal Inspectors must be U.S. citizens.
Candidates to become Postal Inspectors must be aged 21–37.
Candidates to become Postal Inspectors must possess a four-year degree.
Candidates to become Postal Inspectors must meet physical requirements.
Hired Postal Inspectors must complete a 16-week training program.
Postal Inspector openings are posted on the USPIS Careers page.
The USPIS is one of the oldest federal law enforcement agencies.
The USPIS is tasked with ensuring public trust in the mail.
The USPIS includes Postal Inspectors.
The USPIS includes uniformed Postal Police Officers.
Uniformed Postal Police Officers protect postal facilities.
